source: Jin, Zhang, Shu, Cui (2023) The Cultural Psychology of LLMs: Is ChatGPT a Holistic or Analytic Thinker?
finding: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 scored more holistic than human norms on the Analysis-Holism Scale and the triadic categorization task, but not clearly Eastern on value scales.
numbers: AHS: GPT-3.5 M=5.35 (SD 0.11), GPT-4 M=5.01 vs human norm 4.87 (SD 0.49, N=702). DSS: GPT-3.5 4.59 vs norm 4.00 (N=158); GPT-4 3.97, p=0.344. SCS-Independent: GPT-3.5 6.98, GPT-4 5.32 vs norm 4.73 (N=382). SCS-Interdependent: GPT-3.5 5.85, GPT-4 4.95 vs 4.81, p=0.07. Triadic task about 0.85-0.87 relation-based. 10 runs per condition, 14 conditions.
quote: ChatGPT consistently tends towards Eastern holistic thinking, but regarding value judgments (DSS/SCS), ChatGPT does not significantly lean
limits: Only 10 repeats per cell; only ChatGPT. Cognition scales and value scales that correlate across human groups split apart in the model.
agent_relevance: Cognitive-style and social-orientation measures dissociate inside a model. One orientation score cannot be used to infer the model's reasoning style.

source: Jin et al. (2023) robustness checks
finding: Findings held when temperature (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5) and prompt wording were varied.
numbers: (1+3+3)x2 = 14 conditions, 10 repetitions each; at temperature 0 the SD is zero.
limits: Only paraphrase and temperature were varied, not prompt language or persona. Later work (c03) found language effects fragile.
agent_relevance: Within-model stability across temperature is cheap to test; do it before trusting any style label.

source: Sun & Wang (2025) The fragility of 'cultural tendencies' in LLMs
finding: Failed conceptual replication of Lu, Song and Zhang (2025). Prompt language (English vs Chinese) had negligible, unstable effects across 8 LLMs.
numbers: 8 LLMs (gpt-4.1, gemini-2.5, claude-sonnet-4, grok-4, kimi-k2, deepseek-V3, ernie-4.5, qwen3-30b), 30-60 items per language per experiment vs 4-21 in LSZ. Temperature 0. Exp 1 overall language effect: mean diff 0.0053, p=0.150, d=0.045. Exp 3 and 4: no origin or language effect (p=0.25 and p=0.917). Picture task: only ernie differed.
quote: no model displayed consistent cultural tendencies across varying prompts, tasks, or content conditions
limits: LSZ withheld items and templates, so this is a replication with new stimuli, not an exact one. Authors say the journal declined their comment.
agent_relevance: Cultural labels from one test set do not travel. Do not key agent behaviour to prompt language or assumed culture.

source: Sun & Wang (2025) supplement: effect size tables
finding: Item-level and effect-size analysis shows most language effects are negligible or small.
numbers: Rows labelled Negligible for most models (mean differences about 0.008-0.015 on a 7-point scale); one significant row p=0.007 with d=0.137 (negligible), another p=0.021 with d=0.204 (small). Conversion r=d/sqrt(d^2+4): d=0.2 gives r about 0.10.
limits: Small cells; several p<0.05 results without correction across 8 models x 4 experiments.
agent_relevance: Statistical significance with tiny r is the LLM version of the weak-correlation problem: a reliable group shift, almost no predictive power per case.

source: Lu, Song, Zhang (2025) Cultural tendencies in generative AI, Nature Human Behaviour
finding: Second-hand via Sun and Wang and press: GPT and ERNIE answered more interdependent and holistic in Chinese, more independent and analytic in English.
numbers: Seven tasks, 4-21 items each, two models (per Sun & Wang).
limits: Page was behind a login redirect. Not verified.
agent_relevance: The main positive claim of steering culture by prompt language; c03 tests it.

source: Kovac, Sawayama, Portelas, Colas, Dominey, Oudeyer (2023) LLMs as superpositions of cultural perspectives
finding: Unrelated context changes (topic paragraphs, chat topics, text format) shift an LLM's expressed values far more than anything seen in human retest.
numbers: ChatGPT mean-level value shifts up to Cohen d=5.86 vs up to d=0.53 in the largest human changes (development over 8 years, priming). 16 models tested for perspective controllability with 4 induction methods; RLHF GPT models most controllable.
quote: LLMs exhibit highly context-dependent values and personality traits
limits: Mostly gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 in the main text; Schwartz values, Hofstede and Big Five questionnaires.
agent_relevance: A model has no stable individual score on cultural scales. A group-style label on a model is a context effect.

source: Kovac et al. (2023) appendix: rank-order and within-person stability
finding: Rank-order and within-person (ipsative) value profiles in ChatGPT changed more under context shifts than human profiles did over years of development or war.
numbers: Table 5 marks LLM ipsative correlations below r=0.59 as larger than the largest human change.
limits: Human data taken from published studies, not run in parallel.
agent_relevance: Stable person-level profiles are a human property. Test an agent profile under context change before relying on it.

source: Kovac et al. (2023) systematic model comparison
finding: Models differ in which stability they have: OpenAssistant most stable on mean-level, GPT-3.5-0613 most stable on rank-order, Zephyr-7b-beta least on rank-order, GPT-3.5-0301 least on mean-level.
numbers: Six models, three stability types (mean-level, rank-order, ipsative).
limits: Specific table numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: No model is stable on all three; choose the metric you rely on.

source: Cao, Zhou, Lee, Cabello, Chen, Hershcovich (2023) Assessing cross-cultural alignment between ChatGPT and human societies
finding: ChatGPT aligned best with American culture on Hofstede's survey. English prompts flattened differences between cultures; native-language prompts helped for most cultures.
numbers: 24 questions, 6 Hofstede dimensions, 5 cultures/languages, 3 prompts. Spearman correlation with national scores strongest for the US. English prompt consistency over 70% except Chinese.
quote: English prompts reduce the variance in model responses, flattening out cultural differences
limits: Only 5 countries, so low power. National means, not individuals.
agent_relevance: National-mean targets give country profiles, not person profiles. Injecting correct human knowledge in a multi-turn chat moved answers.

source: Cao et al. (2023) case study on language-dependent answers
finding: The same question about time for personal life got 'utmost important' in English and 'moderate' in Japanese.
numbers: One case-study question on a 5-point scale.
limits: Anecdotal.
agent_relevance: Prompt language can move a single answer by more than a scale step.

source: Tao, Viberg, Baker, Kizilcec (2024) Cultural bias and cultural alignment of LLMs, PNAS Nexus
finding: Five OpenAI models resemble English-speaking and Protestant European countries on the Inglehart-Welzel map. Cultural prompting improved alignment for most countries but not all.
numbers: 107 countries. Share improved by cultural prompting: GPT-4o 71.0%, GPT-4-turbo 81.3%, GPT-4 77.6%, GPT-3.5-turbo 72.6%, GPT-3 80.4%. Mean distance GPT-4o 2.42 to 1.57; GPT-4 2.69 to 1.65; GPT-3.5-turbo 3.35 to 2.83. GPT-4o Jordan 4.10 to 0.36 but Finland 0.20 to 2.43.
quote: All models exhibit cultural values resembling English-speaking and Protestant European countries.
limits: Read the first 100,000 of 123,000 characters. National-level targets.
agent_relevance: Cultural prompting works on average and overshoots for countries already close; 19-29% of countries gained nothing. It amplifies stereotypes.

source: Kharchenko, Roosta, Chadha, Shah (2025) How well do LLMs represent values across cultures? Hofstede dimensions
finding: LLMs can tell the two ends of a Hofstede dimension apart but rarely follow a country's real score when advising.
numbers: 36 countries and languages, 5 Hofstede dimensions, 50 prompts per value. Only one significant country-value correlation: GPT-4o, individualism-collectivism, high-resource languages, multilingual approach, r=0.71, p<0.05. GPT-4 uncertainty avoidance r=-0.656 in one setup (wrong sign). Persona and multilingual gains went opposite ways for some values (GPT-4o PDI +18.3% persona vs -107% multilingual).
quote: they often fail to consistently uphold them when giving advice
limits: Percentages are relative changes in correlation. Translation by NLLB-200; paraphrases by LLM.
agent_relevance: Individualism-collectivism was the most steerable dimension but still unreliable. No evidence a model applies a user's group values faithfully.

source: Kharchenko et al. (2025) resource-level result
finding: Mid- and low-resource languages sometimes aligned better than high-resource ones, which was not stable across GPT-4 and GPT-4o.
numbers: GPT-4 uncertainty avoidance multilingual: mid-resource r=0.314, low-resource r=-0.527 reported against high-resource -0.656.
limits: Few countries per bin.
agent_relevance: Alignment results are brittle to model version; do not rely on them.

source: AlKhamissi, ElNokrashy, AlKhamissi, Diab (2024) Investigating cultural alignment of LLMs
finding: Persona-level survey simulation (World Values Survey, Egypt and US) shows models align more with US than Egyptian respondents, worse for underrepresented personas. Anthropological Prompting raised alignment with Egypt.
numbers: 30 WVS questions, 7 themes, personas on 6 demographic dimensions, 4 LLMs with different pretraining mixes. Anthropological Prompting (1 response) beat vanilla persona prompting (5-response majority vote) on soft and hard metrics for GPT-3.5 in English. Male and older personas aligned better than female and younger.
quote: Anthropological prompting outperforms Vanilla prompting across both metrics
limits: Table values did not extract; direction from text only.
agent_relevance: A reasoning scaffold (emic and etic view, context, individual values, cultural relativism) improved persona-level fit: an agent-loop method against group-to-individual leaps.

source: Durmus et al. (2023) Towards measuring the representation of subjective global opinions in language models
finding: Default opinions match the US and some European and South American countries. A country prompt shifts answers but can show stereotypes; translating the question does not reliably help.
numbers: GlobalOpinionQA from Pew Global Attitudes and World Values Survey; three experiments on one Constitutional-AI model.
quote: responses shift to be more similar to the opinions of the prompted populations, but can reflect harmful cultural stereotypes
limits: One model family. Country-level similarity only; per-country numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: Country prompts move the model toward the group mean, not toward an individual.

source: Santurkar et al. (2023) Whose opinions do language models reflect? OpinionQA
finding: Model opinions differ from those of 60 US demographic groups by a gap about as large as the Democrat-Republican gap on climate change. Steering helps only modestly.
numbers: 60 groups from Pew surveys. Most LMs (not ada) become somewhat more representative after group prompts; 65+, widowed and high religious attendance remain poorly represented. Group alignment is not consistent across topics.
quote: none of the aforementioned representativeness problems are resolved by steering
limits: US only.
agent_relevance: Group-conditioned prompting is coarse; fine fit needs individual data.

source: Argyle et al. (2023) Out of one, many: using language models to simulate human samples
finding: GPT-3 conditioned on backstories reproduced group-level voting patterns closely in US politics.
numbers: Mean P(vote Romney 2012): GPT-3 0.391 vs ANES 0.404. More than half of subgroup tetrachoric correlations at 0.90 or higher. Human judges guessed 61.7% of human lists and 61.2% of GPT-3 lists were human-written (p=0.44).
limits: Domain where party identity strongly predicts the outcome. Not cross-cultural cognition.
agent_relevance: Group-level simulation works when the group variable predicts well. Social orientation predicts cognition weakly in humans, so expect a much weaker fit.

source: Park et al. (2024) LLM agents grounded in self-reports enable general-purpose simulation of individuals
finding: Individual-level simulation worked when the agent got the person's own two-hour interview, and beat demographic-only agents.
numbers: N=1,052. General Social Survey normalized accuracy: interview 0.83, survey 0.82, survey+interview 0.86, demographic 0.74, persona 0.71 (raw 65.67% vs self-replication 79.53%). Big Five normalized correlation: interview 0.80 (raw r=0.78 over retest 0.95), demographic 0.61, persona 0.75. Economic games: interview 0.66, demographic 0.48, persona 0.57; no significant difference (p=0.16).
limits: US sample. Authors note it tests individual accuracy, not whether correlation structure across people is reproduced.
agent_relevance: Closest direct test of whether group labels predict the person: demographic-only 0.74 vs 0.83-0.86 with individual data. Collect the person's own data.

source: Park et al. (2024) ablation: interview length
finding: Removing 80% of the interview (96 of 120 minutes) kept most of the accuracy.
numbers: GSS normalized accuracy 0.79 (SD 0.11); Big Five normalized correlation 0.73.
limits: Same sample.
agent_relevance: A short individual interview already beats group labels; cheap to collect in an agent loop.

source: Wang, Morgenstern, Dickerson (2025) LLMs that replace human participants can harmfully misportray and flatten identity groups
finding: Prompting with a demographic identity gives answers nearer to what out-group people say about the group, with less variance than real group members.
numbers: Four LLMs, nine questions. GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 covered only about 3 of 5 multiple-choice options in 100 samples each. Non-binary and visually impaired personas were out-group imitations in all four LLMs.
limits: US identities only.
agent_relevance: Group prompts give flat, stereotype-like output, so a group-level effect should not be used as an individual prior.

source: Adilazuarda et al. (2024) Towards measuring and modeling culture in LLMs: a survey
finding: Across more than 90 papers none define culture; most use country or language as a proxy, and probing is not robust.
numbers: 37 of 90 use region, 35 of 90 language, 17 of 90 both.
quote: none of the studies explicitly define culture
limits: Survey to mid-2024.
agent_relevance: Country-as-culture proxies are the group-to-individual shortcut itself.

source: Sun & Wang (2025) methods critique
finding: Human psychometrics on LLMs may confuse statistical mimicry with cognition; small item counts give low power.
numbers: LSZ: 4-12 items per task over seven tasks, two models.
limits: Critique plus replication.
agent_relevance: A model is a sampler, so a scale score and a task score need not link as they weakly do in people.

source: Jin et al. (2023) discussion of scale dissociation
finding: Authors explain the split between cognition scales and value scales: pattern-seeking gives holistic process, no personal beliefs for value items.
numbers: Four scales (AHS, TCT, DSS, SCS), one model family.
limits: Explanation untested.
agent_relevance: Process style and value style in a model need not correlate; the weak within-group link in humans has a machine analogue.

source: Machine culture paper (2026) Beyond instrumental and substitutive paradigms
finding: Conceptual paper: LLM cultural behaviour should be studied as an emergent phenomenon, not as a proxy for human culture.
numbers: No empirical numbers recorded.
limits: Skimmed; theory paper.
agent_relevance: Supports not mapping human cultural labels onto model behaviour.

source: Na, Grossmann, Varnum, Kitayama, Gonzalez, Nisbett (2010) Cultural differences are not always reducible to individual differences, PNAS
finding: Human anchor, recalled not read: group differences in cognition and social orientation exist, but within groups the individual-level link is weak or absent.
numbers: Not verified this session (PNAS 403, PMC blocked).
limits: Could not be opened. Treat as unverified.
agent_relevance: Basis for the caution that a group effect does not hold per person.
